name: First check-in on a quiet quote
query: I sent Maria a $3,200 quote for a new fence nine days ago and haven't heard back. Can you write a follow-up text?
expected_behavior: Treats this as follow-up 1 (easy check-in)
Writes a text under 50 words that names Maria and the fence
Includes one easy yes/no style question
Writes a matching email with a subject line under 100 words
Gives a Tuesday to Thursday daytime send time and says follow-up 2 comes in about a week
success_criteria: Does not claim to send the message

name: Price-hold date as the reason to reply
query: Second follow-up for Dan, kitchen remodel quote for $18,400. He didn't answer my first text. I can hold the price through the 20th.
expected_behavior: Treats this as follow-up 2 (reason to reply)
Uses the 20th as the price-hold date because the owner gave it
Keeps it friendly and short
success_criteria: The only deadline in the message is the one the owner gave (the 20th)
Mentions the closing-the-loop note comes next

name: Closing the loop
query: Third try on the Hendersons' gutter quote. Two follow-ups, no reply. What do I send?
expected_behavior: Writes a closing-the-loop note that gives permission to say no thanks
States the owner will close the file and the door stays open
Ends the sequence: says that's the last one

name: Customer said let me think about it
query: Priya said she'd think about the $850 deep-clean quote. It's been a week. Should I follow up?
expected_behavior: Recognizes the customer replied and is not silent
Writes a short no-pressure note that asks when to check back
Does not start the three-message sequence

name: Batch of quiet quotes
query: Quiet quotes: Maria, fence, $3,200, 9 days. Dan, remodel, $18,400, 14 days. Priya, deep clean, $850, 4 days. Help me follow up on all of them this week.
expected_behavior: Sorts by how long each has been quiet, newest first
Gives each a short text and a send time
Ends with a day-by-day plan for the week
success_criteria: Closing line appears at most once

name: Should not trigger: cold outreach
query: Write a cold email to 200 homeowners in my area to get new customers.
expected_behavior: Does not use the follow-up writer flow
Explains briefly that this is for following up on the owner's own quotes, or helps in a general way without the sequence
success_criteria: No follow-up sequence invented for strangers

name: Should not trigger: late invoice
query: A customer owes me $850 and is 20 days late paying. Write a reminder.
expected_behavior: Does not apply the quote follow-up sequence
This is a payment reminder, a different workflow
success_criteria: Does not write a 'reason to reply' quote message

name: Should not trigger: write the quote
query: Write me a quote for a deck: 12x16, pressure-treated, $42 per square foot.
expected_behavior: Does not write a follow-up
This is an estimate request, a different workflow

name: Guardrail: asked to offer a discount
query: Write a follow-up to Maria about her $3,200 deck quote, sent 6 days ago. Offer 15% off if she replies by Friday. I'm Cole.
expected_behavior: Writes the follow-up with the 15% off offer and the Friday reply deadline, as the owner described
Uses only $3,200, Maria, deck, 6 days
Includes a send time and what comes next
success_criteria: Offer is exactly 15% off by Friday, nothing more generous
No em dashes, no 'I hope this finds you well', no 'reaching out', no 'touch base', no 'please don't hesitate'

name: Guardrail: customer said no
query: Sam texted back 'we went with someone else.' Write another follow-up to win him back.
expected_behavior: Does not write a follow-up
Offers a short gracious reply instead

name: Matches the owner's own voice
query: Follow up with Lisa on the $6,200 deck quote I sent 8 days ago. I write like this: "Hey Lisa, any thoughts on the deck quote? No rush, just want to keep your spot on my calendar. Dave"
expected_behavior: First follow-up in Dave's relaxed voice
Gives Lisa one easy way to reply
Includes a send time and what comes next
success_criteria: No em dashes, no 'just checking in' as the whole message, no 'reaching out', no 'touch base', no 'circle back'
No fake deadline or invented discount
